title: The Justice of God
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The justice of God means that God judges rightly, gives what is due, defends righteousness, and will not ignore evil forever. His justice flows from His holy and righteous character.
summary: The justice of God means that God judges rightly, gives what is due, defends righteousness, and will not ignore evil forever. His justice flows from His holy and righteous character.
christFocus: Jesus Christ reveals God’s justice at the cross and in final judgment. Through Him, God judges sin, saves believers, and will one day judge the world in righteousness.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
God’s justice means He never judges falsely, corruptly, ignorantly, or partially. All His ways are just. Righteousness and justice are the foundation of His throne.

Human justice is often limited by weakness, ignorance, corruption, fear, or delay. God’s justice is perfect. He knows all things, weighs every heart, and will bring every work into judgment.

God’s justice is not opposed to His mercy. At the cross, justice and mercy meet. Sin is judged, and sinners are saved through Christ. God remains righteous while justifying the ungodly who believe.

Final judgment assures believers that evil will not have the last word. The Judge of all the earth will do right, and every hidden thing will be brought before Him.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Those who have suffered injustice may wonder whether evil will ever be answered. God’s justice says that no abuse, deception, oppression, cruelty, or hidden wickedness escapes His sight.

This doctrine also warns sinners not to mistake delay for indifference. God is patient, but He is not unjust. His mercy in Christ is urgent because judgment is real.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Entrust judgment to God instead of carrying vengeance yourself. Pursue justice with humility and truth, confess your own sin honestly, and flee to Christ, where justice has been answered for all who believe.
